name: Chassahowitzka River: Main Spring, Seven Sisters and Baird Creek
area: 8600 W Miss Maggie Drive, Chassahowitzka, Citrus County
coordinateNote: Florida DEP coastal-paddling map set Segment 7 Map 2B lists Chassahowitzka River Campground access A at 28.7150, -82.5771; this is the public launch area, not a spring vent. Approximation uses the area/address in the listed location source; not a measured or geocoded entrance.
navigationDestination: Chassahowitzka River Campground, 8600 W Miss Maggie Drive, Homosassa FL
experience: Seven Sisters' limestone spring holes, the narrow Baird Creek paddle to The Crack, and possible dolphins, manatees and otters make this a varied wildlife-and-water outing. The operator offers a Springs & Swim tour through November 14; the exact stops depend on tides, boat traffic and conditions. Main Spring, Seven Sisters, Crab Creek and The Crack are distinct stops in the Chassahowitzka system.
duration: Allow half a day; tides, route and skill determine actual reach.
cost: Campground operator lists single kayak $35/day, tandem $45, SUP $50 plus tax; parking $5 without trailer/$7 with trailer.
access: Launch at the Chassahowitzka public ramp or book an operator's kayak tour. Get Up and Go lists a Springs & Swim tour April 1–November 14 and a winter manatee tour November 15–March 31. The advertised swimming stops are surface-water activities; underwater tunnels are not part of this recommendation. Rental and parking charges depend on the provider.

conditions.summary: Published rental/launch service; shallow/tidal channels can change access. No same-day clarity, flow or swim-zone confirmation.

water: SWFWMD says tides and fresh/brackish sources vary across nearby springs. No guarantee of clear water on trip dates.
mobility: Launch transfer and sustained paddle; shallow side channels may limit access. Stay in surface/open water within qualification.
